35006-an-experimental-translocation-of-t.title: An Experimental Translocation Of The Eastern Timber Wolf
35006-an-experimental-translocation-of-t.creator: Unknown
35006-an-experimental-translocation-of-t.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Two male and two female eastern timber wolves (_Canis lupus lycaon_), live-trapped in Minnesota were released in March 1974 near Huron Mountain in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Their movements were monitored by aerial radio-telemetry.

arxiv-2109-05149.title: Extract, Integrate, Compete: Towards Verification Style Reading Comprehension
arxiv-2109-05149.creator: Chen Zhang, Yuxuan Lai, Yansong Feng, Dongyan Zhao
arxiv-2109-05149.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a new verification style reading comprehension dataset named VGaokao from Chinese Language tests of Gaokao. Different from existing efforts, the new dataset is originally designed for native speakers’ evaluation, thus requiring more advanced language understanding skills.

arxiv-2112-07024.title: Detecting inhomogeneous chiral condensation from the bosonic two-point function in the ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional Gross-Neveu model in the mean-field approximation
arxiv-2112-07024.creator: Adrian Koenigstein, Laurin Pannullo, Stefan Rechenberger, Martin J. Steil, Marc Winstel
arxiv-2112-07024.description: Abstract The phase diagram of the ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional Gross-Neveu model is reanalyzed for (non-)zero chemical potential and (non-)zero temperature within the mean-field approximation. By investigating the momentum dependence of the bosonic two-point function, the well-known second-order phase transition from the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} symmetric phase to the so-called inhomogeneous phase is detected.

arxiv-2205-07485.title: Aspects of two-photon absorption of squeezed light: the CW limit
arxiv-2205-07485.creator: C. Drago, J. E. Sipe
arxiv-2205-07485.description: Abstract We present a theoretical analysis of two-photon absorption of classical and squeezed light valid when one-photon absorption to an intermediate state is either resonant or far-detuned from resonance, and in both the low and high intensity regimes. In this paper we concentrate on continuous-wave excitation, although the approach we develop is more general.

arxiv-2402-11630.title: Towards Distributed and Intelligent Integrated Sensing and Communications for 6G Networks Thanks: This work has been supported by the SNS JU project 6G-DISAC under the EU’s Horizon Europe research and innovation Program under Grant Agreement No 101139130.
arxiv-2402-11630.creator: Emilio Calvanese Strinati, George C. Alexandropoulos, Navid Amani, Maurizio Crozzoli
arxiv-2402-11630.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emilio Calvanese Strinati, George C. Alexandropoulos, Navid Amani, Maurizio Crozzoli. This paper introduces the DISAC ( DISAC ) concept, a transformative approach for 6G wireless networks that extends the emerging concept of ISAC ( ISAC ).

arxiv-2404-07226.title: Houston we have a Divergence: A Subgroup Performance Analysis of ASR Models
arxiv-2404-07226.creator: Alkis Koudounas, Flavio Giobergia
arxiv-2404-07226.description: Abstract I Abstract The Fearless Steps APOLLO Community Resource [ 1 ] provides an unparalleled opportunity to explore the vast potential of historical multi-speaker team communications from the NASA Apollo missions. This study focuses on discovering which are the characteristics that make Apollo recordings more or less intelligible to Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) methods.

arxiv-2503-20128.title: Active magneto gyrator as a tunable heat engine or heat pump
arxiv-2503-20128.creator: F. Adersh, M. Muhsin, M. Sahoo
arxiv-2503-20128.description: Abstract We theoretically investigate the thermodynamic performance characteristics of an active magneto-gyrator taking into account the two-dimensional motion of an inertial charged active particle confined in an asymmetric parabolic potential and in contact with two heat baths kept at two different temperatures. A magnetic field of constant magnitude is applied in a direction perpendicular to the plane of motion.

arxiv-2509-12130.title: Notebook for the CheckThat! Lab at CLEF 2025
arxiv-2509-12130.creator: Ariana Sahitaj, Jiaao Li, Pia Wenzel Neves, Fedor Splitt, Premtim Sahitaj, Charlott Jakob, Veronika Solopova, Vera Schmitt
arxiv-2509-12130.description: Abstract This notebook reports the XplaiNLP submission to the CheckThat! 2025 shared task Alam et al. 2025 on multilingual subjectivity detection. We evaluate two approaches: (1) supervised fine-tuning of transformer encoders, EuroBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, and German-BERT, on monolingual and machine-translated training data; and (2) zero-shot prompting using two LLMs: o3-mini for Annotation (rule-based labelling) and gpt-4.

arxiv-2601-11846.title: The Third VoicePrivacy Challenge: Preserving Emotional Expressiveness and Linguistic Content in Voice Anonymization
arxiv-2601-11846.creator: Natalia Tomashenko, Xiaoxiao Miao, Pierre Champion, Sarina Meyer, Michele Panariello, Xin Wang, Nicholas Evans, Emmanuel Vincent, Junichi Yamagishi, Massimiliano Todisco
arxiv-2601-11846.description: Abstract We present results and analyses from the third VoicePrivacy Challenge held in 2024, which focuses on advancing voice anonymization technologies. The task was to develop a voice anonymization system for speech data that conceals a speaker’s voice identity while preserving linguistic content and emotional state.

arxiv-2602-14330.title: Pattern recognition with superconducting wirelet neurons
arxiv-2602-14330.creator: Khalil Harrabi 1,2, Leonardo R. Cadorim 3 & Milorad V. Milošević 3
arxiv-2602-14330.description: Abstract Neuromorphic computing aims to reproduce the energy efficiency and adaptability of biological intelligence in hardware. Superconducting devices are an attractive platform due to their ultra-low dissipation and fast switching dynamics. Here we introduce a shunted superconducting wirelet as an artificial neuron, representing the simplest possible superconducting neuron implementation.

pmc-10739327.title: An update: is there a relationship between H. pylori infection and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease? why is this subject of interest?
pmc-10739327.creator: Xingcen Chen, Ruyi Peng, Dongzi Peng, Jia Xiao, Deliang Liu, Rong Li
pmc-10739327.description: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is thought to impact various extragastric diseases, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), the most common chronic liver disease. Meanwhile, the pathogenesis of NAFLD needs further research, and effective treatment for this disease remains elusive. In this mini-review, we enumerate and ponder on the evidence demonstrating an association between H. pylori infection and NAFLD.

pmc-10800487.title: The neonatal adverse event severity scale: current status, a stakeholders' assessment, and future perspectives
pmc-10800487.creator: Karel Allegaert, Thomas Salaets, Kelly Wade, Mary A. Short, Robert Ward, Kanwaljit Singh, Mark A. Turner, Jonathan M. Davis, Tamorah Lewis
pmc-10800487.description: To support informed decisions on drug registration and prescription, clinical trials need tools to assess the efficacy and safety signals related to a given therapeutic intervention. Standardized assessment facilitates reproducibility of results. Furthermore, it enables weighted comparison between different interventions, instrumental to facilitate shared decisions.

pmc-11321590.title: The forgotten p-versine and p-coversine family of functions revisited
pmc-11321590.creator: Ali Hamzah Alibrahim, Saptarshi Das
pmc-11321590.description: This study delves into special class of generalized p-trigonometric functions, examining their connection to the established counterparts like p-cosine and p-sine functions. We here explore the new class of functions called the p-versine, p-coversine, p-haversine, and p-hacovercosine, by providing comprehensive definitions and properties. Grounded in the characteristics of p-cosine and p-sine functions, the newly proposed functions offer unique mathematical insights.

pmc-11433642.title: Physicochemical Characterization of Ca- and Cu-Decorated TiO2 Microparticles and Investigation of Their Antimicrobial Properties
pmc-11433642.creator: Andreea Neacsu, Viorel Chihaia, Razvan Bucuresteanu, Anton Ficai, Roxana Doina Trusca, Vasile-Adrian Surdu, Adela Nicolaev, Bogdan Cojocaru, Monica Ionita, Ioan Calinescu, Viorica Parvulescu, Lia-Mara Ditu
pmc-11433642.description: Ca- and Cu-decorated TiO2 microparticles are titanium dioxide nanoparticles that have been decorated with calcium and copper ions. TiO2, CaO, and CuO are low-cost, non-toxic, and non-hazardous materials. The aim of the present study was the physicochemical characterization of Ca- and Cu-decorated TiO2 microparticles and the evaluation of their antimicrobial activity.

pmc-11434399.title: Lipid-Lowering Treatment Gaps in Patients after Acute Myocardial Infarction: Using Global Database TriNetX
pmc-11434399.creator: Grete Talviste, Mall Leinsalu, Peeter Ross, Margus Viigimaa, Vilnis Dzerve, Mauro Feola, Aivars Lejnieks
pmc-11434399.description: Background and Objectives: Patients with previous acute myocardial infarction are at significantly higher risk of recurrent events. Early and intensive lipid-lowering therapy targeting low-density lipoprotein cholesterol is a key strategy for reducing cardiovascular risk in post-acute myocardial infarction patients worldwide.

pmc-12445565.title: Scedosporium infection as a late complication after start of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor: two case reports

pmc-12445565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highly effective modulator treatment (HEMT) has resulted in an improved prognosis for people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF). pmc-12619074.creator: Ellen ANDREASSON, Jörgen SÖVERSTAD, Inka LÖFVENMARK
pmc-12619074.description: ObjectivesTo describe the prevalence of -shoulder pain and associations with patient characteristics and activities of daily living in individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) and to identify pain--relieving strategies. This paper presents questionnaire results from a larger study that also includes clinical and ultrasound assessments.DesignCross-sectional study.ParticipantsIndividuals with SCI for at least 1 year.

pmc-12654815.title: Tackling Conifer Needle Cast and Ash Dieback with Host-Derived Microbial Antagonists Exhibiting Plant Growth-Promoting Traits
pmc-12654815.creator: Milana Šilanskienė, Dorotėja Vaitiekūnaitė, Vaida Sirgedaitė-Polikaitienė
pmc-12654815.description: Needle cast (Lophodermium seditiosum Minter, Staley & Millar) in Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.) and European ash (Fraxinus excelsior L.) dieback (Hymenoscyphus fraxineus (T. Kowalski) Baral, Queloz & Hosoya) are among the most destructive forest and tree plantation diseases in Europe, threatening not only targeted plant species but also the whole ecosystem.

pmc-12681981.title: Immunotherapy versus lenvatinib in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: The critical role of subgroup analyses
pmc-12681981.creator: Tingfeng Huang, Jiahao Law, Ningqi Pang, Shichuan Tang
pmc-12681981.description: atment of advanced HCC with the introduction of various systemic therapies, including lenvatinib and regimens based on immune checkpoint inhibitors. However, a critical question remains: How to compare the relative effectiveness of immunotherapy versus multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitors in real-world populations, thereby providing evidence for personalized first-line treatment decisions across different etiologies and patient subgroups.

pmc-12986178.title: Pseudoacacia Honey of Hungarian and Slovak Origin: Selected Quality Parameters and Antioxidant Capacity
pmc-12986178.creator: Diana Stehlíková, Ágnes Farkas, Rita Filep, Nóra Papp, Dragica Purger, Jaroslav Tóth, Szilvia Czigle
pmc-12986178.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The pseudoacacia species (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) are flowering plants that produce nectar and can be the sources of unifloral honey. Robinia is native to North America and is invasive in several European countries. The aim of this work was to determine and compare the physicochemical parameters, proline content, and antioxidant capacity of pseudoacacia honey collected from different locations in two central European countries (Hungary and Slovakia). The botanical origin of each honey sample was verified by melissopalynological analysis.

pmc-13136895.title: Nuclear genome profiling of two species of Epidendrum (Orchidaceae): genome size, repeatome, and ploidy
pmc-13136895.creator: Miguel A Alcalá-Gaxiola, Gerardo A Salazar, Eric Hágsater, Mónica A Flores-Iniestres, Lidia I Cabrera, Aldo I Aviña-Rivera, Pedro Mercado-Ruaro, Susana Magallon, Carolina Granados Mendoza, Aleida Núñez-Ruiz, Gloria Soldevila, Araxi O Urrutia, Rubi N Meza-Lázaro
pmc-13136895.description: Characterizing genomic properties such as genome size, ploidy level, heterozygosity, and repetitive DNA proportion and composition without relying on genome assembly is crucial for profiling the genomes of non-model species. This study compares genome profiles of Epidendrum anisatum and Epidendrum marmoratum, using flow cytometry and k-mer analysis approaches, as well as bioinformatic ploidy-level estimation and repeatome characterization.

pmc-13388777.title: Functional hydrogel biomaterials for urological diagnosis and treatment—design strategies and application progress: a review
pmc-13388777.creator: Kuntai Li, Huichong Yu
pmc-13388777.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In urology, the treatment of diseases such as bladder cancer, urethral stricture, and benign prostatic hyperplasia faces challenges such as short drug retention time, unstable therapeutic effects, and drug resistance. Traditional treatments, such as surgery, systemic drug therapy, and local drug instillation, although controlling the condition to some extent, still have many limitations, necessitating new localized treatment and precise diagnostic strategies. Hydrogels have made significant progress in urology, especially in the fields of drug delivery, disease diagnosis, and tissue repair.

pmc-13486341.title: Overexpression of cryIAb gene for enhancing yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas) resistance using a marker-free double T-DNA system in Rojolele of Indonesia Rice cultivar
pmc-13486341.creator: Agus Rachmat, Enny Rimita Sembiring, Ade Nena Nurhasanah, Nurul Fitriah, Vincentia Esti Windiastri, Eva Erdayani, Rumella Simarmata, Inez HS Loedin, Sri Indrayani, Carla Frieda Pantouw, Siti Halimah Larengkeng, Enung Sri Mulyaningsih
pmc-13486341.description: The aromatic rice cultivar Rojolele (Oryza sativa L. cv. Rojolele), prized for its superior organoleptic qualities, is highly susceptible to yellow stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas), a pest causing significant yield losses in Asia. To address this vulnerability, we developed marker-free transgenic Rojolele lines expressing the cry1Ab gene using a double T-DNA vector system, eliminating reliance on antibiotic resistance markers.
